requirements.title: GitLab Client Construction, Lifecycle, and Factory Wiring
requirements.rationale: Direct construction and factory integration allow callers to instantiate authenticated or unauthenticated GitLab adapters configured for public or self-hosted instances.

criteria.action: provide a GitLab client adapter struct that implements every method of the Client interface and export the NewGitLab(Options) (Client, error) constructor
criteria.contract: gitlabClient implements the issuex.Client interface completely; Authenticated() returns true when holding a non-empty token and false otherwise; Close() closes idle transport connections and returns nil

setup: the issuex package and GitLab client adapter implementation
check.pseudocode:
var _ issuex.Client = (*gitlabClient)(nil)
c := newTestGitLabClient(Options{Token: "glpat_secret"})
assert c.Authenticated() == true
assert c.Close() == nil

unauth := newTestGitLabClient(Options{})
assert unauth.Authenticated() == false

criteria.condition: NewGitLab is called with Options
criteria.action: resolve BaseURL from Options or GITLAB_API_URL or default to https://gitlab.com/api/v4 with trailing slashes trimmed and /api/v4 appended when absent, Token from Options or GITLAB_TOKEN, HTTPClient from Options or default 30-second timeout client, and UserAgent from Options or default agent-fox
criteria.contract: BaseURL resolves from Options or GITLAB_API_URL or defaults to https://gitlab.com/api/v4 with trailing slashes trimmed and /api/v4 appended when absent; Token resolves from Options or GITLAB_TOKEN; default HTTPClient has a 30-second timeout if unspecified; default UserAgent is agent-fox if unspecified

setup: custom Options and process environment variable combinations
check.pseudocode:
c1, _ := NewGitLab(Options{BaseURL: "https://gitlab.example.com/subpath/", Token: "tok1", UserAgent: "custom-ua"})
assert c1.(*gitlabClient).baseURL == "https://gitlab.example.com/subpath/api/v4"
assert c1.(*gitlabClient).token == "tok1"
assert c1.(*gitlabClient).userAgent == "custom-ua"

t.Setenv("GITLAB_API_URL", "https://gl.corp/api/v4/")
t.Setenv("GITLAB_TOKEN", "tok2")
c2, _ := NewGitLab(Options{})
assert c2.(*gitlabClient).baseURL == "https://gl.corp/api/v4"
assert c2.(*gitlabClient).token == "tok2"
assert c2.(*gitlabClient).userAgent == "agent-fox"
assert c2.(*gitlabClient).httpClient.Timeout == 30*time.Second

criteria.condition: NewWithOptions is called with NoOp set to false and the resolved forge type is ForgeTypeGitLab
criteria.action: construct and return the GitLab client adapter instead of returning ErrUnsupportedForge
criteria.contract: NewWithOptions detects ForgeTypeGitLab and returns an active GitLab client adapter rather than ErrUnsupportedForge

setup: Options with remote URL pointing to gitlab.com and NoOp false
check.pseudocode:
client, err := issuex.NewWithOptions(issuex.Options{
    Repo: issuex.Repo{Owner: "group/subgroup", Name: "project"},
    RemoteURL: "https://gitlab.com/group/subgroup/project.git",
    Token: "glpat-token",

criteria.action: issue GET /api/v4/version to probe for a GitLab self-hosted instance before returning ErrAmbiguousForge
criteria.contract: NewWithOptions issues GET /api/v4/version to probe the host, constructing a GitLab client if successful or returning ErrAmbiguousForge if the probe fails

criteria.action: report true from Authenticated() when holding a non-empty token and false otherwise, and close idle HTTP connections on the underlying transport from Close() returning nil

for any outgoing HTTP request, include Accept: application/json and User-Agent headers, appending PRIVATE-TOKEN: <Token> when authenticated and Content-Type: application/json when a request body is present
criteria.contract: Accept header is always application/json; User-Agent is always populated; PRIVATE-TOKEN header is set when authenticated and omitted when unauthenticated; Content-Type is application/json when request body is present

requirements.title: Project Metadata and URL-Encoded Path Resolution
requirements.rationale: Project metadata inspection verifies project accessibility, permissions, default branch, and allowed merge strategies using URL-encoded paths without extra ID lookups.

criteria.action: for any project-scoped REST endpoint, format the target project path as url.PathEscape(repo.String()) with slashes replaced by %2F without executing numeric project ID lookups
criteria.contract: the project path segment in the URL is url.PathEscape(repo.String()) with all slashes converted to %2F without executing numeric project ID lookups

setup: a quickcheck generator for Repo instances with single-level or nested group owner paths

criteria.condition: GetRepository is called with a valid Repo
criteria.action: execute GET /projects/{project_path} and populate a Repository struct with FullName from path_with_namespace, DefaultBranch, Private based on visibility, Archived, and Permissions computed from effective access level
criteria.contract: FullName, DefaultBranch, Private based on visibility, Archived, and Permissions computed from effective access level are returned; merge settings merge_method and squash_option are recorded in the client

setup: a mock server returning GitLab project JSON with visibility, access levels, and merge settings
check.pseudocode:
srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    assert r.Method == "GET"
    assert r.URL.Path == "/api/v4/projects/group%2Fproject"
    w.Write([]byte(`{
        "path_with_namespace": "group/project",
        "default_branch": "main",
        "visibility": "private",
        "archived": false,
        "permissions": {
            "project_access": {"access_level": 30},
            "group_access": {"access_level": 20}
        },
        "merge_method": "merge",
        "squash_option": "default_on"
    }`))
}))
defer srv.Close()
c := newTestGitLabClient(Options{BaseURL: srv.URL, Token: "glpat-tok"})
repo, err := c.GetRepository(context.Background(), Repo{Owner: "group", Name: "project"})
assert err == nil
assert repo.FullName == "group/project"
assert repo.DefaultBranch == "main"
assert repo.Private == true
assert repo.Archived == false
assert repo.Permissions.Push == true && repo.Permissions.Pull == true && repo.Permissions.Admin == false
assert c.mergeMethod == "merge" && c.squashOption == "default_on"

criteria.condition: GetRepository receives a successful project response
criteria.action: record the project merge settings merge_method and squash_option for pull request merge resolution

requirements.title: Issue Lifecycle and Retrieval
requirements.rationale: Issue lifecycle methods enable creating, reading with comment history, updating, closing, and filtered listing of GitLab issues with normalized state values.

criteria.condition: CreateIssue is called with a Repo and CreateIssueRequest on an authenticated client
criteria.action: execute POST /projects/{project_path}/issues with title, description, and labels, returning the created Issue with Number set to iid, Title, Body, State normalized to open, URL, Author, Labels, timestamps, and IsPR set to false
criteria.contract: POST /projects/{project_path}/issues is executed with title, description, and labels; created Issue is returned with Number set to iid, State normalized to open, and IsPR set to false

setup: a mock server handling issue PUT requests and comment creation
check.pseudocode:
var updatedBody string
var stateEvent string
var postedComment string

srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    if r.Method == "POST" && strings.HasSuffix(r.URL.Path, "/notes") {
        var req map[string]any
        json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req)
        postedComment = req["body"].(string)
        w.WriteHeader(http.StatusCreated)
        w.Write([]byte(`{"id": 10, "web_url": "https://gitlab.com/n/10"}`))
        return
    }
    if r.Method == "PUT" && strings.HasSuffix(r.URL.Path, "/issues/12") {
        var req map[string]any
        json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req)
        if desc, ok := req["description"].(string); ok { updatedBody = desc }
        if se, ok := req["state_event"].(string); ok { stateEvent = se }
        w.Write([]byte(`{"iid": 12, "title": "T", "description": "new body", "state": "closed", "author": {"username": "u"}}`))
        return
    }
}))
defer srv.Close()

c := newTestGitLabClient(Options{BaseURL: srv.URL, Token: "tok"})
ref := IssueRef{Repo: Repo{Owner: "org", Name: "repo"}, Number: 12}
newBody := "new body"
iss, err := c.UpdateIssue(context.Background(), ref, UpdateIssueRequest{Body: &newBody})
assert err == nil
assert iss.Body == "new body"

errClose := c.CloseIssue(context.Background(), ref, "resolved in v2")
assert errClose == nil
assert postedComment == "resolved in v2"
assert stateEvent == "close"

setup: a mock server returning HTTP 201, HTTP 409, or HTTP 400 with 'already exists' message
check.pseudocode:
srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    var req map[string]any
    json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req)
    assert strings.HasPrefix(req["color"].(string), "#")
    name := req["name"].(string)
    if name == "existing-409" {
        w.WriteHeader(http.StatusConflict)
        w.Write([]byte(`{"message": "Label already exists"}`))
        return
    }
    if name == "existing-400" {
        w.WriteHeader(http.StatusBadRequest)
        w.Write([]byte(`{"message": "Label already exists"}`))
        return
    }
    w.WriteHeader(http.StatusCreated)
    w.Write([]byte(`{"id": 100, "name": "new-label", "color": "#FF0000"}`))
}))
defer srv.Close()

c := newTestGitLabClient(Options{BaseURL: srv.URL, Token: "tok"})
repo := Repo{Owner: "org", Name: "repo"}

assert c.CreateLabel(context.Background(), repo, Label{Name: "new-label", Color: "FF0000"}) == nil
assert c.CreateLabel(context.Background(), repo, Label{Name: "existing-409", Color: "#FF0000"}) == nil
assert c.CreateLabel(context.Background(), repo, Label{Name: "existing-400", Color: "#FF0000"}) == nil

setup: a mock server handling merge PUT requests returning 200, 405, 406, or 409
check.pseudocode:
srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    var req map[string]any
    json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req)
    if req["commit_message"] == "conflict" {
        w.WriteHeader(http.StatusConflict)
        w.Write([]byte(`{"message": "Branch cannot be merged"}`))
        return
    }
    if req["commit_message"] == "method_not_allowed" {
        w.WriteHeader(http.StatusMethodNotAllowed)
        w.Write([]byte(`{"message": "405 Method Not Allowed"}`))
        return
    }
    w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
    w.Write([]byte(`{"sha": "mergesha999", "merge_commit_sha": "mergesha999"}`))
}))
defer srv.Close()

c := newTestGitLabClient(Options{BaseURL: srv.URL, Token: "tok"})
ref := IssueRef{Repo: Repo{Owner: "org", Name: "repo"}, Number: 1}

res, err := c.MergePullRequest(context.Background(), ref, MergeOptions{
    Method: MergeMethodSquash, CommitMessage: "merge commit", SHA: "head123",
})
assert err == nil
assert res.Merged == true
assert res.SHA == "mergesha999"

_, errConflict := c.MergePullRequest(context.Background(), ref, MergeOptions{CommitMessage: "conflict"})
assert IsConflict(errConflict) == true

_, err405 := c.MergePullRequest(context.Background(), ref, MergeOptions{CommitMessage: "method_not_allowed"})
assert IsConflict(err405) == true

cUnauth := newTestGitLabClient(Options{})
_, errUnauth := cUnauth.MergePullRequest(context.Background(), ref, MergeOptions{})
assert IsNoToken(errUnauth) == true
errPostUnauth := cUnauth.PostReviewComment(context.Background(), ref, "body")
assert IsNoToken(errPostUnauth) == true

requirements.title: GitLab REST Transport, Error Handling, and Rate Limiting
requirements.rationale: Bounded memory usage, rate-limit backoff with retry, and canonical error classification ensure resilience against GitLab API failures and throttling.

criteria.action: read all HTTP response bodies through an io.LimitReader bounded to at most 8 MB (8388608 bytes)
criteria.contract: response body reading is capped at exactly 8 MB (8388608 bytes) preventing out-of-memory exhaustion

setup: a mock server returning an HTTP response body exceeding 8 MB (8,388,608 bytes)
check.pseudocode:
bigPayload := strings.Repeat("A", 9*1024*1024)
srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    w.Write([]byte(bigPayload))
}))
defer srv.Close()

c := newTestGitLabClient(Options{BaseURL: srv.URL, Token: "tok"})
body, err := c.do(context.Background(), "GET", "/test", nil, nil)
assert err == nil
assert len(body) == 8*1024*1024

criteria.condition: an HTTP response has status 429 and the calculated RetryAfter backoff duration is less than or equal to 120 seconds
criteria.action: invoke the configured sleep function for the backoff duration and retry the request once
criteria.contract: when Retry-After <= 120s, custom sleep function is invoked with backoff duration and request is retried once; when Retry-After > 120s or retried request fails, returns an error satisfying IsRateLimited(err) == true

setup: a mock server returning HTTP 429 with Retry-After header and a client configured with custom sleep function
check.pseudocode:
var sleepDurations []time.Duration
mockSleep := func(d time.Duration) {
    sleepDurations = append(sleepDurations, d)
}

calls := 0
srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    calls++
    if r.URL.Path == "/retry-ok" && calls == 1 {
        w.Header().Set("Retry-After", "10")
        w.WriteHeader(http.StatusTooManyRequests)
        w.Write([]byte(`{"message": "Rate limit exceeded"}`))
        return
    }
    if r.URL.Path == "/retry-fail" {
        w.Header().Set("Retry-After", "5")
        w.WriteHeader(http.StatusTooManyRequests)
        w.Write([]byte(`{"message": "Rate limit exceeded"}`))
        return
    }
    if r.URL.Path == "/retry-excessive" {
        w.Header().Set("Retry-After", "125")
        w.WriteHeader(http.StatusTooManyRequests)
        w.Write([]byte(`{"message": "Rate limit exceeded"}`))
        return
    }
    w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
    w.Write([]byte(`{"status": "ok"}`))
}))
defer srv.Close()

c := newTestGitLabClient(Options{BaseURL: srv.URL, Token: "tok"})
c.sleep = mockSleep

calls = 0
_, err1 := c.do(context.Background(), "GET", "/retry-ok", nil, nil)
assert err1 == nil
assert len(sleepDurations) == 1 && sleepDurations[0] == 10*time.Second

_, err2 := c.do(context.Background(), "GET", "/retry-excessive", nil, nil)
assert IsRateLimited(err2) == true

_, err3 := c.do(context.Background(), "GET", "/retry-fail", nil, nil)
assert IsRateLimited(err3) == true

criteria.condition: an HTTP response returns status 404, 405, 406, or 409
criteria.action: wrap the corresponding sentinel error ErrNotFound for status 404 or ErrConflict for status 405, 406, and 409 in the returned HTTPError
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 response returns an error satisfying IsNotFound(err) == true; HTTP 405, 406, and 409 responses return errors satisfying IsConflict(err) == true

setup: a mock server returning HTTP status codes 404, 405, 406, and 409
check.pseudocode:
srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    switch r.URL.Path {
    case "/404": w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNotFound); w.Write([]byte(`{"message": "not found"}`))
    case "/405": w.WriteHeader(http.StatusMethodNotAllowed); w.Write([]byte(`{"message": "method not allowed"}`))
    case "/406": w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNotAcceptable); w.Write([]byte(`{"message": "not acceptable"}`))
    case "/409": w.WriteHeader(http.StatusConflict); w.Write([]byte(`{"message": "conflict"}`))
    }
}))
defer srv.Close()

c := newTestGitLabClient(Options{BaseURL: srv.URL, Token: "tok"})
_, err404 := c.do(context.Background(), "GET", "/404", nil, nil)
assert IsNotFound(err404) == true

_, err405 := c.do(context.Background(), "GET", "/405", nil, nil)
assert IsConflict(err405) == true

_, err406 := c.do(context.Background(), "GET", "/406", nil, nil)
assert IsConflict(err406) == true

_, err409 := c.do(context.Background(), "GET", "/409", nil, nil)
assert IsConflict(err409) == true
